study_id: Lehr et al. - 2024 - Differential effects of donor factors on post-transplant survival in lung transplantation

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult lung transplant recipients and uses a random forest machine learning model (non‑linear AI) to predict post‑transplant survival, meeting population, intervention, outcome, and study design criteria.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: National Institutes of Health (NIH) and Cystic Fibrosis Foundation
identification_methods.Setting: Analysis of US Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) data
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective registry study evaluating donor factor interactions on post‑transplant survival in adult bilateral lung transplant recipients.
identification_methods.Institution: Cleveland Clinic, Department of Pulmonary Medicine
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult primary bilateral lung transplant recipients (n=7,609); excluded single lung transplants.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Cox proportional hazards regression, Random Forest
identification_methods.Input Variables: Recipient age, sex, diagnosis group; donor factors including age, sex, race/ethnicity, smoking history, diabetes, CMV/EBV mismatch, cause of death, ischemic time, etc.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Univariable and multivariable Cox models with interaction terms; backward elimination for variable reduction; random forest model built for comparison; model performance assessed via AUC, Brier score, calibration plots.

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult primary bilateral lung transplant recipients
population.Population Notes: Data from US Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients, adult bilateral lung transplants between 19 Feb 2015 and 1 Feb 2020

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: SRTR registry clinical variables (donor and recipient characteristics)
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data with time-dependent AUC evaluation
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Four models built: COX, COX+PT-CAS, RF, RF+PT-CAS; compared to PT-CAS using discrimination (AUC) and calibration
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Interactions between donor and recipient factors examined; modest improvement in prediction when adding donor factors
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: COX+PT-CAS model AUC 0.626 at 1 year vs PT-CAS AUC 0.609; similar trends at 3 and 5 years
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All primary bilateral lung transplant recipients (n=7,609)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Addition of donor factors yielded only modest improvement in discrimination and calibration
